translationRepairs: Zhuangzong’s Empress Jing Shenmin, Lady Liu, came from Cheng’an in Weizhou.
Zhuangzong’s Empress Shenminjing, Lady Liu, came from Cheng’an in Weizhou.
神閔敬皇后 is the posthumous title Shenminjing; Jing Shenmin reverses the three title characters.
Zhuangzong’s Empress Jing Shenmin, the Liu clan, was a native of Cheng’an in Weizhou.
Zhuangzong’s Empress Shenminjing, of the Liu clan, was a native of Cheng’an in Weizhou.
The literal field has the same reversed title; 神閔敬 must be Shenminjing.
Lady Han and the others seethed; Han was made Shufei and Yi Defei.
Lady Han and the others seethed; Han was made Shufei and Yi was made Defei.
韓氏為淑妃，伊氏為德妃 separately enfeoffs each woman; “Yi Defei” fuses person and title, while “Yi was made Defei” keeps the parallel.
Wen Tao of Xuzhou, courting her piety, offered his mansion as a temple for her merit.
Wen Tao of Xu Prefecture, courting her piety, offered his mansion as a temple for her merit.
許州節度使 is Xu Prefecture (Xuchang), not 徐州; Xuzhou is a different place.
The military governor of Xuzhou, Wen Tao, because the empress was devoted to Buddhism, asked to make his private residence a monastery to bless her.
The military governor of Xu Prefecture, Wen Tao, because the empress was devoted to Buddhism, asked to make his private residence a monastery to bless her.
The literal likewise misreads 許州 as Xuzhou; Xu Prefecture matches the Chinese.

In autumn of Tongguang 3 floods ravaged the Yellow River country; refugees clogged the roads, taxes failed, soldiers starved, and next year’s rent was collected early while Zhuangzong and the empress still hunted.

In autumn of Tongguang 3 floods ravaged the two He regions; refugees clogged the roads, taxes failed, soldiers starved, and next year’s rent was collected early while Zhuangzong and the empress still hunted.
兩河 denotes the two He regions as a historical term, not the vague “Yellow River country.”
He left two sons: Sibi and Sigu.
He left two sons: Sibi and Sigong.
嗣肱 is Sìgōng; 肱 is gōng, so Sigu is a misreading.
The literal repeats the same misromanization of 嗣肱 as Sigu.
Sigu was bold; under Zhou Dewei he won many fights and became chief adjutant of horse and foot.
Sigong was bold; under Zhou Dewei he won many fights and became chief adjutant of horse and foot.
嗣肱 opens this unit; the subject must be Sigong, not Sigu.
Sigu in youth had daring and strategy; following Zhou Dewei he won many battles and was made chief adjutant of horse and foot.
Sigong in youth had daring and strategy; following Zhou Dewei he won many battles and was made chief adjutant of horse and foot.
Same 嗣肱→Sigong correction in the literal field.
At Hubi, with Li Cunshen’s victory, Sigu took a Liang general.
At Hubi, with Li Cunshen’s victory, Sigong took a Liang general.
嗣肱獲梁將 names Sigong as the capturer, not Sigu.
When Li Cunshen defeated Liang at Hubi, Sigu captured a Liang general.
When Li Cunshen defeated Liang at Hubi, Sigong captured a Liang general.
The literal likewise requires Sigong for 嗣肱.
When Liang besieged Zhuo, Sigu relieved it with Cunshen; his merit was greatest and he became prefect of Wei and commander north of Yanmen.
When Liang besieged Tiao, Sigong relieved it with Cunshen; his merit was greatest and he became prefect of Yu and commander north of Yanmen.
蓚縣 is Tiao (not Zhuo), 嗣肱 is Sigong, and 蔚州 is Yu (not Wei); the proposed after corrects all three.
When Liang’s Taizu besieged Zhuo, Sigu followed Cunshen to relieve it; the Liang army withdrew; Sigu’s merit was greatest; he was promoted to prefect of Wei and commander north of Yanmen.
When Liang’s Taizu besieged Tiao, Sigong followed Cunshen to relieve it; the Liang army withdrew; Sigong’s merit was greatest; he was promoted to prefect of Yu and commander north of Yanmen.
The literal has the same three errors—Zhuo/Sigu/Wei for 蓚/嗣肱/蔚—and the proposed after fixes them.
Wang Yu of Xin rebelled to the Khitan; Sigu recovered Ji, Ru, and Wu and became prefect of Xin and commissioner of the northern mountains.
Wang Yu of Xin rebelled to the Khitan; Sigong recovered Ji, Ru, and Wu and became prefect of Xin and commissioner of the northern mountains.
嗣肱取媯、儒、武 again requires Sigong, not Sigu.

Wang Yu of Xinzhou rebelled against Jin and fled to the Khitan; the mountain posts all rebelled; Sigu took Ji, Ru, and Wu and was made prefect of Xin and regimental commissioner of the northern mountains.

Wang Yu of Xinzhou rebelled against Jin and fled to the Khitan; the mountain posts all rebelled; Sigong took Ji, Ru, and Wu and was made prefect of Xin and regimental commissioner of the northern mountains.
Same Sigong correction for 嗣肱 in the literal field.
From the wars with Helian Duo and Li Keyong through exile among the Tatars and the campaign against Huang Chao, Kening always marched with him.
From the wars with Helian Duo and Li Keju through exile among the Tatars and the campaign against Huang Chao, Kening always marched with him.
李可舉 is Li Keju; Li Keyong (李克用) is Taizu himself and cannot be the opponent named here.
When Taizu fought Helian Duo and Li Keyong between Yun and Wei, later fled to the Tatars, entered to break Huang Chao, Kening never failed to follow.
When Taizu fought Helian Duo and Li Keju between Yun and Yu, later fled to the Tatars, entered to break Huang Chao, Kening never failed to follow.
Literal likewise needs Li Keju for 李可舉, and 雲、蔚 are Yun and Yu, not Yun and Wei.
Cunmei was Prince of Yong, Cunba Prince of Yong, Cunli Prince of Xue, Cunwo Prince of Shen, Cunyi Prince of Mu, Cunque Prince of Tong, Cunji Prince of Ya.
Cunmei was Prince of Yong, Cunba Prince Yong, Cunli Prince of Xue, Cunwo Prince of Shen, Cunyi Prince of Mu, Cunque Prince of Tong, Cunji Prince of Ya.
邕王 and 永王 are distinct fiefs; the proposal’s Chinese parentheticals are disallowed in English, so split them as Prince of Yong (邕王, Cunmei) versus Prince Yong (永王, Cunba).
Cunmei was Prince of Yong, Cunba Prince of Yong, Cunli Prince of Xue, Cunwo Prince of Shen, Cunyi Prince of Mu, Cunque Prince of Tong, Cunji Prince of Ya.
Cunmei was Prince of Yong, Cunba Prince Yong, Cunli Prince of Xue, Cunwo Prince of Shen, Cunyi Prince of Mu, Cunque Prince of Tong, Cunji Prince of Ya.
Literal likewise collapses 邕王 and 永王; use English-only Prince of Yong versus Prince Yong without Chinese graphs.
Your merit is great and Father once gave you the realm—I beg you take the command until I can stand alone."
Uncle’s merit and virtue are both high; the late king once entrusted you with government—I dare trouble my younger uncle with the army and government until I can stand on my own."
叔父 and 季父 identify Kening as Zhuangzong’s younger uncle; the idiomatic omission loses that kinship, which the proposed after restores.
He became acting Grand Preceptor and co-equal with the Secretariat.
He became acting Grand Commandant and co-equal with the Secretariat.
檢校太尉 is acting Grand Commandant; Grand Preceptor would be 太師.
He was promoted to acting Grand Preceptor and co-equal with the Secretariat.
He was promoted to acting Grand Commandant and co-equal with the Secretariat.
The literal repeats the 太尉/太師 confusion; Grand Commandant is correct.
Jiji told Chongtao: “Father trusts you as Yi Yin and Huo Guang—he will not leave you in the wilds.
Jiji told Chongtao: “His Majesty relies on the Palace Attendant as on Mount Heng and Mount Hua—he will not leave you in the wilds.
陛下 is His Majesty, 侍中 is Palace Attendant, and 衡、華 are Mount Heng and Mount Hua—not Father or Yi Yin and Huo Guang.

Jiji told Chongtao: “His Majesty relies on you as on Yi Yin and Huo Guang, honors you above the temple, expecting you to pacify all under Heaven and master the four barbarians—surely he will not abandon an elder in barbarian lands.

Jiji told Chongtao: “His Majesty relies on the Palace Attendant as on Mount Heng and Mount Hua, honors you above the temple, expecting you to pacify all under Heaven and master the four barbarians—surely he will not abandon an elder in barbarian lands.
The literal’s Yi Yin and Huo Guang invent persons for 衡、華; Mount Heng and Mount Hua match the metaphor.
Shu was new; bandits roamed; Chongtao delayed withdrawal while Ren Yuan pacified the hills.

The two Sichuans were newly pacified; Meng Zhixiang had not yet arrived; bandits still gathered in the hills; Chongtao was sending Ren Yuan and others to recruit them, fearing later trouble, so the army did not return at once.
兩川新定、孟知祥未至、分出招集 are omitted or distorted in the compressed idiomatic; the proposed after restores those facts.

As Yan’gui was about to go he saw Empress Liu: “I heard from Yansi that affairs in Shu are already beyond remedy; disaster will strike in an instant—how can one go three thousand li back and forth for orders from the granary!”

As Yan’gui was about to go he saw Empress Liu: “I heard from Yansi that affairs in Shu are already beyond remedy; disaster will strike in an instant—how can one go three thousand li back and forth awaiting orders!”
往復廩命 means going back and forth to await/receive orders; “orders from the granary” is a false literalization of 廩.
Jiji had been castrated young and left no sons.
From youth Jiji suffered a eunuch-like affliction and left no sons.
少病閹 is a eunuch-like affliction from youth, not proven surgical castration; the proposed wording matches the Chinese.
Hearing Chongtao might stay, Zhuangzong sent Xiang Yansi to hurry withdrawal.
Hearing that Chongtao wished to remain in Shu, Zhuangzong was also displeased and sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to urge Jiji to withdraw the army.
亦不悅、宦者、趣繼岌班師、留蜀 are all in the Chinese and missing from the compressed idiomatic; the after restores them.
